citation: Alexander AS, Nitz DA (2017). Spatially periodic activation patterns of retrosplenial cortex encode route sub-spaces and distance traveled. Curr Biol 27:1551-1560
environment_type: closed plus-shaped track with recurrent segments
environment_size: Closed plus-shaped track run clockwise, 12 equal segments; Fig. 1B labels one segment 55 cm, so a lap is about 660 cm (derived, nominal; rats cut the corners, Fig. 1B right); 1 cm edges, open view of the room; reward at the arrow point. measure: Spearman correlation of odd vs even trial population rate vectors at all pairs of route positions (Fig. 1C); mean r by separation read here
normalization: Spearman (rank) correlation across cells; per-cell normalization of the vectors not stated (Fig. 1C left shows max-normalized profiles)
simultaneous_or_pooled: pooled: one 229-cell vector across 5 rats and all sessions; the 5 to 140 cell resampling belongs to the distance analysis of Fig. 4F
dist_r05_cm: not reached (mean r >= 0.71 at all separations up to 650 cm)
floor: about 0.77 (mean r at 100 to 300 cm); minimum about 0.72 near 480 to 500 cm
far_behaviour: Peak 0.91 (0.93 under the tick-label calibration) beside the diagonal; r = 0.88, 0.83 and 0.79 at 27, 55 and 82 cm; half of the drop to the floor (r about 0.84) at about 45 cm; a dip to 0.78 at about 120 cm, then a shallow local maximum of 0.79 at 165 to 182 cm (one quarter route, 3 segments), about 0.01 above the dip, a dip to 0.74 near 280 to 290 cm and a second rise to 0.78 at about 360 to 385 cm; the global minimum, 0.71 to 0.72, lies near 480 to 500 cm; the matrix corners (start against end of the lap, the same place on the closed track) read about 0.75 to 0.76, no higher than the floor. CA1 matrices lack the off-diagonal repeats (Fig. 1D; alexander2017_k2)
location: p. 1552 (Fig. 1B-D); pp. 1557-1558 (Discussion); STAR Methods pp. e3-e4
quote_or_reading: "Unlike matrices for the CA1 ensemble, off-diagonal correlations for RSC ensembles exhibited repeating patterns across the track, indicating the presence of a sub-population of RSC neurons having repeating patterns over quarter and/or half sections of the full route" (pp. 1552-1553); "although strong population correlations were observed between analogous positions of route sub-spaces, the strongest ensemble correlation values across odd versus even trials occurred at similar full-route positions" (pp. 1557-1558). Reconstruction error RSC "1.9 ± 2.7 cm", CA1 "5.2 ± 6.7 cm mean ± SEM" (141 CA1 place cells, 3 rats). Fig. 1 raster 1339 x 1617 px (xref 64) extracted from the PDF; matrices 512 x 512 px; Spearman bar in the raster with tick labels 1 and 0.5; each pixel mapped to the nearest bar colour, black turn lines and the white peak line masked; r averaged by |row - column| in 4 cm steps; 660 cm per matrix side; script kernel_an17.py. Two calibrations: bar ends = 1 and 0.5, or tick-label centres = 1 and 0.5 (bar then spans 0.48 to 1.03); values below give both where they differ.
notes: Within one environment and session (odd vs even laps). The kernel has a narrow peak on a high floor and aliases at same-shape segments. The floor probably reflects broad, continuous RSC firing in vectors with no stated per-cell normalization, so the r = 0.5 width is undefined rather than large (inference). The distance reconstruction is Fig. 4 (not Fig. 6): first-half and mirrored second-half vectors around a symmetry point, error 2.93 cm in RSC against 12.61 cm in CA1 (not 2.09 cm); it measures distance from the symmetry point, not a kernel. Distances assume 55 cm segments; corner cutting may make them up to about 10% high.
